clue.text: Others arrived, carrying buckets, heading only for seaside resort

parts.note: more as in 'more people', others besides

indicators.note: a word that carries something holds it inside itself, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: past tense of come

indicators.note: a heading is what stands at the top, so only the first letter of the following word is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of buckets

explanation.surface: Day-trippers turn up with buckets, all bound for the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: MORE then CAME carrying B gives MORECAMBE. Morecambe is a seaside town on the Lancashire coast in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Morecambe is a traditional English holiday town on the coast of Morecambe Bay.

clue.text: Cutting and juicing lemon can make one nearly blind

indicators.note: juicing a fruit pulps and mashes it, so the remaining letters get rearranged
cutting something trims it, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written, then trimmed and mixed

explanation.surface: Lemon juice squirting in your eye can leave you nearly blind.
explanation.walkthrough: LEMON cut short is LEMO, which rearranges to MOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Moles live underground and have very poor eyesight, the proverbial 'blind as a mole'.

clue.text: Do this to get a rope for Tommy?

definitions.text: Do this to get a rope
definitions.meaning: surface: an instruction for obtaining some cord
setter's reading: shake up the five letters of a sung drama and you get 'a rope'; Tommy is the Who's famous example of the genre

explanation.surface: Instructions for finding a rope for someone called Tommy.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: ROCK the word OPERA (shake its letters) and you get A ROPE. Tommy (1969), by the Who, is the classic ROCK OPERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tommy is a celebrated example of a rock opera, a story told through a sequence of rock songs.

clue.text: Tea carried by postman along with one piece of bread

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
Postman Pat, the children's TV character
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The postman brings the tea and a slice of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, tea 'carried by' the postman sits on top of him. Postman Pat is a British children's TV series about a village postman.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapati is a flat unleavened Indian bread, so one is a piece of bread.

clue.text: When, in 2024, we celebrated Easter parade

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Easter Sunday 2024 fell on 31st of this month
second meaning: to walk in formation

explanation.surface: An Easter parade, as held in 2024.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter 2024 fell at the very end of the third month, and the verb means to walk in step as on a parade.

clue.text: Filename is 'Dicky', student admitted casually

indicators.note: something admitted is let in, so one piece is placed inside the other
dicky means unsound or shaky, so the letters are in poor order and need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A computer file has been dodgily named, with a student casually let in.
explanation.walkthrough: Add L to FILENAME and rearrange all nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: En famille is French for 'in the family', describing something done informally, at home, without ceremony.

clue.text: Hail American sitcom once last part is released

indicators.note: releasing the final part lets it go, so the closing letter is dropped

parts.note: the Boston bar sitcom of the 1980s

explanation.surface: Praise for an old US sitcom once its final episode airs.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheers loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To hail someone is to greet or acclaim them, which is to cheer them.

clue.text: Clear the end of chapel during lively seance

indicators.note: something during an event happens within it, so one piece goes inside
lively suggests bouncing about, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: last letter of chapel

explanation.surface: Spirits are cleared from a chapel during an animated seance.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes into SEANCE, and the seven letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleanse is to make clean, or to clear something of impurities.

clue.text: More old art is put up

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting a word up makes it read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: More antique art is hung on the wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, which is what more means as an adjective.

clue.text: Communist putsch ultimately going wrong provides futile diversion

parts.note: red is a standard term for a communist

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the preceding word is kept

parts.note: last letter of putsch
erring means straying or going wrong

explanation.surface: A communist coup that collapses only distracts from the real issue.
explanation.definitionFit: A red herring is a false lead that draws attention away from what matters, so a pointless distraction.

clue.text: Tight-fitting material wedged in smelly crack

indicators.note: something wedged in is lodged inside other words, so the answer sits within the next phrase

parts.note: sitting across the two words

explanation.surface: Tight sportswear riding up somewhere unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Lycra is the trademark stretchy fabric used for close-fitting clothing such as cycling shorts.

clue.text: Repton's head chose to house fellow, and perhaps made pupils slip up

indicators.note: a head is at the front, so the first letter of the school's name is taken

parts.note: first letter of Repton, an English public school

indicators.note: housing something means giving it room inside

parts.note: elected means chose, as in a vote
F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: A school head appoints a fellow, which makes the pupils misbehave.
explanation.walkthrough: R then ELECTED around F. The definition is a picture: read PUPILS backwards, as in a mirror, and it becomes SLIP UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To reflect is to give a mirror image, and a mirror reversal of the word pupils spells slip up, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Salt, and where it's kept when hot

parts.note: salt is kept in a pot
as in 'as I arrived', meaning when
H for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Where salt is stored when the kitchen is hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Potash is a potassium salt, chiefly potassium carbonate, once made from wood ash in pots.

clue.text: Order soldier to lead engagement

parts.note: a man is a private soldier, as in officers and men
a date is an appointment

explanation.surface: A command for a soldier to head into battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandate is an official order or commission to act.

clue.text: 'Up you come doctor' said a spy with binoculars

parts.note: OO looks like a pair of binocular lenses

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered

explanation.surface: A spy with binoculars reports a doctor cheerfully helping a patient up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like the person being addressed, but it is the anagram signal; binoculars are drawn as two round lenses side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Oops-a-daisy is said when helping someone, often a child, who has fallen get back up.

clue.text: Monumental arrangement of lobelias — about 100

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters surround a number
an arrangement puts things in a new order, as with flowers

parts.note: taken as written
Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A grand floral display of about a hundred lobelias.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeliscal means like an obelisk, a tall stone pillar, so in the form of a monument.

clue.text: Vessel of three fellows held up by substantial support

parts.note: CO for colleague or fellow, then F twice, the abbreviation for fellow
EE cup, a large bra size

explanation.surface: A ship with three men on board, carried on a sturdy base.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, the fellows 'held up by' the support sit above it. CO (as in co-worker) plus F and F make the three fellows; the support is a bra, and EE is a generous British cup size.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffee cup is a drinking vessel, vessel meaning any container for liquid.

clue.text: Naughty youngster taking top off to show boob

indicators.note: removing the top of a word drops its first letter

parts.note: a little terror is a badly behaved child

explanation.surface: A cheeky youth strips off and exposes something rude.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface leans on boob as a body part; here it means a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A boob is British slang for a silly mistake, so it is a blunder or slip.

clue.text: Dreaded movement of a star exploding miles above one

indicators.note: above in a down clue means placed over, so the earlier parts sit on top of the letter for one
exploding means blown apart, so the letters of a star are scattered into a new order

parts.note: far means a long way, many miles off
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An astronomical picture: a star exploding many miles above someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreaded' is a pun: the Rastafari movement is known for dreadlocks, not for being feared.
explanation.definitionFit: Rastafari is a Jamaican religious movement whose followers often wear dreadlocks, so it is a dreadlocked, or dreaded, movement.

clue.text: Virtuous woman followed by a very loud man

definitions.note: Read as a verb, as in 'man the pumps', meaning to supply people to work something, which is exactly what staffing does.

parts.note: abbreviation for saint, a holy person
taken as written
fortissimo in music notation

explanation.surface: A good woman pursued by a noisy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a noun but works as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To staff a place is to provide workers for it, which is to man it.

clue.text: Start carrying electronic goods

indicators.note: one word carrying another holds it within itself

parts.note: a start is a sudden shock
e- abbreviates electronic, as in email

explanation.surface: Begin shipping electronic merchandise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start' looks like a verb meaning begin; here it is the noun for a jump of alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: Freight is goods carried by lorry, ship or train.

clue.text: One with special shake and complimentary cooked salmon spending pound

parts.note: complimentary means given without charge, so free

indicators.note: cooked suggests something prepared or altered, so the remaining letters are rearranged
spending means paying out and so losing, so the pound letter leaves the fish

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: A recipe in which a milkshake and some free cooked salmon cost a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shake' reads like a drink on a menu, but here it is a handshake: Freemasons are said to greet each other with a secret grip. 'spending pound' takes L from SALMON, and 'cooked' reshapes what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Freemasons are reputed to identify one another with a secret handshake, so a member is one with a special grip.

clue.text: Copper with funny clothing who delivered messages?

indicators.note: clothing something wraps it, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: merry means jolly or amusing
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A police officer in comic dress who used to bring news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' reads as a policeman; it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercury was the Roman messenger god, carrying the gods' messages.

clue.text: Drain with key quietly put inside

indicators.note: a piece put inside goes within the other word

parts.note: the Delete key on a keyboard
p for piano, quietly in music

explanation.surface: Emptying a tank with a key quietly slipped into place.
explanation.definitionFit: To deplete is to drain or use up a supply.

clue.text: Arranged like Russian dolls, 50 fine journalists dance

indicators.note: arranged here describes how the pieces are set out, one held within another

parts.note: PA is the Press Association, a news agency of journalists

indicators.note: Russian dolls nest one inside the next, so each piece sits inside the one around it

parts.note: OK means fine or all right
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty fine reporters, lined up like nesting dolls, break into a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The image of nesting dolls tells the solver that three pieces go one inside another rather than side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: This lively Bohemian couple dance in two-four time is a ballroom staple.

clue.text: Moving article in free daily's opening pages

indicators.note: the single letter A is moved to a different place in the word, a rearrangement

parts.note: spare as in spare time, free

indicators.note: an opening is the start, so the first letter is kept

parts.note: first letter of daily

explanation.surface: A touching feature article opens the centre pages of a free daily paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The article A moves from inside SPARE to its end.
explanation.definitionFit: A spread is a pair of facing pages in a newspaper or magazine, often given over to one feature.

clue.text: Two consecutive notes are discovered from The Sun

parts.note: so and la, neighbours in the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: dis-covered means uncovered, so the outer letters are stripped away leaving the middle

parts.note: the word with its covers removed

explanation.surface: Two musical notes found in a tabloid newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun reads as the British tabloid paper; here it is the star.
explanation.definitionFit: Solar means relating to or derived from the sun.

clue.text: Unknown characters on the radio getting smart

indicators.note: radio is heard not seen, so the spelling follows sound

parts.note: Y is an algebraic unknown, and several of them are Ys

explanation.surface: Mysterious people on a radio show become clever.
explanation.definitionFit: Wise means sensible and knowledgeable, which is what smart means.

clue.text: Sick old American soldier leading around 50? That's silly

parts.note: unwell
standard abbreviation
a GI is a US army private
circa, about
Roman numeral fifty

explanation.surface: An ailing elderly US veteran approaching fifty, which is absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading' simply puts GI ahead of the CA and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Illogical means senseless or lacking reason, which is silly.

clue.text: Taste shown by posh old lady with something dotted

parts.note: U means upper-class
mam is mother
lower-case i carries a dot

explanation.surface: A refined elderly woman with a spotty garment shows her taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Umami is the savoury taste, counted as the fifth basic taste alongside sweet, sour, salty and bitter.

clue.text: It's used when brewing teas drunk after the end of July

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: last letter of July

indicators.note: drunk means unsteady and staggering, so the letters reel into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Teas drunk at the end of July, after a brewing session.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeast is the fungus added in brewing to ferment sugars into alcohol.

clue.text: Something regularly delivered to journalists — cocaine?

definitions.meaning: surface: an official statement handed to the press
setter's reading: a dose of the drug snorted at a celebration

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is the official policy fed to the press, while a 'line' of cocaine taken at a party gives the comic second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A political party's agreed position, repeated to reporters, is its official policy statement; a line is also a dose of powdered drug.
